title-group.article-title: Analytical validation of a hybrid-capture panel for BRCA1/2 and homologous recombination deficiency in ovarian cancer.

contrib-group.aff: Central Oncology Research Hospital, Houston, TX
Westlake Comprehensive Cancer Center, Seattle, WA
Harborview Institute of Oncology, San Diego, CA

abstract.p: Background: Detection of BRCA1/2 alterations and homologous recombination deficiency is clinically relevant in high-grade serous ovarian cancer, but routine testing can be limited by turnaround time, tissue availability, and workflow complexity. We developed and analytically validated a hybrid-capture next-generation sequencing assay for rapid molecular testing. Methods: The assay was designed to detect BRCA1/2 coding regions and 24 homologous recombination genes using formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tissue. Analytical sensitivity, specificity, precision, reproducibility, reportable range, and limit of detection were evaluated with reference materials, contrived specimens, and residual clinical samples. Testing used a minimum input of 40 ng. Orthogonal concordance was assessed against orthogonal sequencing and genomic scar testing. Results: The assay achieved a limit of detection of 2.0% variant allele frequency. Overall analytical sensitivity was 96.4% and analytical specificity was 99.0%. Across 9 independent runs, the median coefficient of variation was 5.9%. Results were reproducible across operators, reagent lots, and instruments. Agreement with orthogonal sequencing and genomic scar testing was 96.1%, with discordant samples concentrated near the analytical detection limit. Conclusions: This hybrid-capture next-generation sequencing assay provides sensitive, specific, and reproducible detection of BRCA1/2 alterations and homologous recombination deficiency in high-grade serous ovarian cancer. The workflow may offer a practical alternative or complement to existing molecular methods when rapid results or limited specimen input are important. Prospective clinical validation is ongoing. Research Sponsor: Women’s Cancer Research Foundation.
